02

Independent challenge toolkit

These focused techniques extend the core Unit 5 patterns without turning the workbook into a textbook.

01

Dictionary get()

get() reads a key and can supply a safe default when the field is optional.

visits = member.get("visits", 0)
02

Filtered summaries

Build a filtered list, then calculate a count, total or average from its records.

active = [r for r in records if r["active"]]
print(len(active))
03

Transaction logs

Append completed actions instead of rewriting the history. Never log passwords.

with open("transactions.txt", "a", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    file.write(record + "\n")
04

Password-strength rules

Check length and character groups before accepting a fictional classroom password.

strong = len(password) >= 8 and any(c.isdigit() for c in password)
05

Safe record updates

Find and validate first. Change memory second. Save the collection last.

record = find_by_id(records, target)
if record is not None:
    record["status"] = "Closed"
    save_records(records)
06

Project modules

Move reusable loading and saving functions into a second Python file when the program becomes large.

from data_tools import load_records, save_records
03

Challenge lab

Choose a larger project, plan its functions and develop it beyond the starter.

    PYTHON LAB REFERENCE
    Support & examples
    Independent challenge reference for multi-file persistent systems.
    Key concepts
    • Load once, process in memory and save after validated changes.
    • Append transaction history instead of replacing it.
    • Keep credentials out of logs and reports.
    • Use separate modules for reusable data functions.
    • Retest by closing and reopening the program.
    Common errors
    • Mixing record formats between files
    • Saving before validation
    • Logging sensitive data
    • Forgetting to include a module in the ZIP
    Misconceptions to avoid
    More files automatically means better structure
    Separate files only when they have clear responsibilities and a predictable interface.
    A successful run proves persistence
    The data must still be correct after the program closes and reloads the files.
    EXAMPLE 01 · SAFE UPDATE
    Validate, change, save
    record = find_record(records, target)
if record and amount <= record["balance"]:
    record["balance"] -= amount
    save_records(records)
    Persistent updates follow a controlled order.
    EXAMPLE 02 · MODULE
    Import file helpers
    from data_tools import load_records, save_records
    The module file must be included in the same project folder.
    EXAMPLE 03 · REPORT
    Summarise filtered records
    active = [r for r in records if r["active"]]
print("Active:", len(active))
    A report turns stored records into useful information.
